title: Ethics Commission penalties: how long after the events, and how large beside the sums described
question: For each penalty the Ethics Commission has issued, how many years passed between the events and the penalty, and how does the penalty compare with the largest sum of money the stipulation describes?
finding: The Commission's file lists 164 penalties from 2003 to 2026, $1.0 million in all; the median is $1,500 and the largest $108,180. A year for the events could be read for 112: the median penalty came 2 years later, 47 came three or more years later and 14 five or more. For example, in case 24-000817 (a candidate's two committees) the count lines add up to $192,216 of prohibited contributions against a penalty of $108,180; and in case 21-22-000463 a commissioner sought a City subcontract the stipulation says was worth more than $2.7 million and was penalised $9,500. The sum is sometimes the amount at issue and often only the size of the campaign, contract or decision around it, so each row prints the words beside the figure.
how: Every record in the Commission's penalty file, with its stipulation text where the document on file has a text layer. The year of the events is the election year in the respondent committee's name where there is one, otherwise the middle year of the written-out dates in the stipulation (dates in the penalty year itself are set aside when there are earlier ones); years is the penalty year less that year. The sum is read by machine: where the stipulation's count lines print sums in brackets, those are added up; otherwise it is the largest dollar figure that appears beside a word of giving, paying, receiving, contracting or reporting and not beside words that mark a legal limit, a range or the penalty itself. Cases for not filing a statement are left out of the sum reading. Rows are ordered by penalty as a share of that sum, smallest first.
limits: The largest sum described is not the Commission's finding of harm or gain, and for most rows it is not the amount of the violation. It may be the whole of a campaign's receipts in a case about a missing disclaimer, the cost of a project a commissioner should not have voted on, money reported late, or contributions refunded before anyone complained; penalties are set by the number and kind of violations, the respondent's record and cooperation, and ability to pay. The machine reading also picks the wrong figure in some documents. The year of the events is an estimate from the dates the document mentions, so years to penalty can be off by a year or two either way, and a long gap can mean the conduct itself ran for years. 53 stipulations are scans with no text and have neither figure. Reading each stipulation is the only way to fix the amount at issue.
